$comment: #EXP-2143 follow-up (Danny, 2026-11-26): NO 'SIGN IN AGAIN' ERROR. An action behind Better Auth's fresh-session gate (`session.freshAge`, default one day since the session's `createdAt`) that is refused with SESSION_NOT_FRESH opens ONE step-up sheet, 'Confirm it's you', in place: the person proves it is them with a way in the account already has, the server marks the SAME session fresh, and the refused action runs again by itself. Never a sign-out, never a new session, never a lost draft (the sheet sits over the form; the form's state is untouched). GATES (`gates`): the only fresh-gated endpoints a client calls are the passkey registration pair; removals and unlinks ride tRPC without the gate (users.ts), `/list-sessions` and `/delete-user` have no client. SERVER (`server`, a Better Auth plugin, lib/auth/step-up.ts): every endpoint needs a real session (an `expu_` key is refused like the identity paths) and never mints a session: on proof it sets the CURRENT session's `createdAt` to now (the value the gate reads) and rewrites the cookie cache. `methods` answers the account's ways in, in this order: `passkey` (the account has one and passkeys are on), `email` (a code to the account's own address; the instance sends mail), `password` (a credential row with a password and passwords are on); empty = nothing to prove with (a provider-only account on an instance without mail): the action fails with `copy.notFresh` as before. PROOF: passkey = the plugin's own `generate-authenticate-options` (its challenge cookie, allowCredentials = the account's passkeys) then `POST /step-up/passkey {response}`: the assertion must verify against a passkey OF THE SESSION'S USER (another account's passkey is refused); email = `POST /step-up/email/send` mails a 6-digit code (hashed at rest, 10 minutes, 5 tries, bound to the session) and `POST /step-up/email/verify {code}`; password = `POST /step-up/password {password}`. Errors carry a code (`errors`). CLIENTS x4 (web lib/step-up + StepUpDialog, desktop domain::step_up, iOS ExpCore StepUp + StepUpSheet, Android domain/StepUp + StepUpSheet): the pure reducer `stepUpReduce(state, event)` replays `flows`. Events: `refused {code, methods}` (the action came back refused; the client reads `methods` once at that moment), `choose {method}`, `submit` (the proof is in flight), `proved`, `rejected {code}` (`CANCELLED` = the person dismissed the system passkey prompt: no error, the sheet stays), `cancel` (the sheet is closed: the action is dropped quietly, no toast, the draft stays), `done` (the resumed action finished). A second SESSION_NOT_FRESH after a proof is never a loop: the action fails with `copy.notFresh`. The sheet opens on `methods[0]`; choosing `email` mails a code at once (a client effect, again on `copy.resend`). Layout x4: the platform's sheet/dialog (web Dialog, iOS sheet, Android ModalBottomSheet), title, the method's one-line description, the method's field (none for passkey), the inline error under it, the other methods as link buttons (`copy.switch`, plus `copy.resend` on the email method), then the one primary button (`copy.confirm`, or `copy.passkey` for the passkey method), pending while `sheet` = busy. Cancel = the platform's own dismissal (web Dialog: Cancel button + Esc/outside; phones: swipe down or back, as on every sheet) = event `cancel`.

copy.title: Confirm it's you

description.email: Enter the code we sent to {email}.

copy.notFresh: Sign in again to do this (your current session is older than a day).

errors.INVALID_OTP: That code is not right. Check the email and try again.
errors.OTP_EXPIRED: That code expired. Request a new one.
errors.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS: Too many attempts. Request a new code.
errors.PASSKEY_FAILED: Couldn't confirm it with that passkey.
errors.default: Couldn't confirm it's you. Try again.

methodCases.name: no passkey starts with the code
passkeys off hides the account's passkeys
passwords off hides a stored one
a provider-only account without mail has nothing

flows.name: web: add passkey, code by email, the add resumes
android: add passkey, a wrong code, then the right one, the add resumes
ios: add passkey, confirmed with the existing passkey, the add resumes and finishes
desktop: switch from the passkey to the password, the action resumes
a wrong password stays open with the error
a dismissed passkey prompt is no error
an unknown failure reads the default
